name: swiftui-drag-to-dismiss-side-drawer
description: Pattern for implementing a drag-to-dismiss side drawer in SwiftUI using DragGesture with callback lifting to parent, GeometryReader-based dismiss threshold, and simultaneous gesture handling to avoid ScrollView conflicts.
when_to_use: When building a SwiftUI side menu or drawer that should respond to a swipe-left drag gesture while also containing a ScrollView. The ScrollView blocks normal .gesture() modifiers, requiring .simultaneousGesture().
workflow_sequences: 1. Add onDragChanged and onDragEnded callbacks to the child drawer view (not @State inside child)
2. Attach .simultaneousGesture(DragGesture(minimumDistance:15)) to the ScrollView inside the drawer
3. In onChanged: filter for horizontal-dominant left drags (dx < 0 && abs(dx) > abs(dy))
4. In parent GeometryReader: compute baseOffset = showMenu ? 0 : -screenWidth
5. Apply .offset(x: baseOffset + dragDelta) to the drawer; suppress animation while dragging (menuDragOffset != 0)
6. On drag end: compare abs(dx) to dismissThreshold (e.g. screenWidth * 0.35); dismiss or snap back with .easeInOut
example_invocations: SideMenuView(isPresented: $showMenu, onDragChanged: { dx in menuDragOffset = dx }, onDragEnded: { dx in if dx < -dismissThreshold { showMenu = false } })
troubleshooting_tips: If the drawer jumps on drag start, ensure dragDelta clamps at 0: min(0, menuDragOffset) for left-slide drawers
If scroll and drag conflict: verify .simultaneousGesture is on ScrollView, not an inner VStack
If dismiss fires immediately: increase minimumDistance (15px is minimum; 20-30px for less sensitive feel)
Suppress spring-back animation during drag: .animation(menuDragOffset == 0 ? .easeInOut : nil, value: menuDragOffset)
